data.gender_notes: Muhazzab is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root h-z-b, meaning to glorify, exalt, or adorn. In Islamic tradition, this name signifies one who is honored, esteemed, and highly regarded. The name Muhazzab carries the meaning “Glorified, Exalted” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muhazzab usually hope their child will grow to embody glorified, exalted and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that reflects the divine attributes of glory and exaltation.
data.etymology: Muhazzab belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Glorified, Exalted.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muhazzab total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: محزاب
in_arabic.meaning: المحزاب هو الشخص الذي يتميز بالحزم و القوة في اتخاذ القرارات
in_arabic.long_meaning: المحزاب مشتق من الجذر 'حَزَبَ' الذي يعني التجمّع أو التآلف. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم المحزاب لوصف الشخص الذي يتميز بالحزم و القوة في اتخاذ القرارات، و هو أيضاً الشخص الذي يلتزم بالحق و العدل. في القرآن الكريم، لا يوجد ذكر صريح لكلمة المحزاب، لكن الجذر 'حَزَبَ' ذُكر في عدة آيات، مثل قوله تعالى: 'وَمَآ أَفَاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرَى فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ كَيْ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الْأَغْنِيَاءِ مِنكُمْ وَمَا آتَاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانتَهُوا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ' (الحشر: 7). و في هذا السياق، يدل المحزاب على الشخص الذي يتحلى بالحزم و الشجاعة في مواجهة التحديات.

in_urdu.name: محزاب
in_urdu.meaning: محزاب وہ شخص ہے جو فیصلے کرنے میں مضبوطی اور پختگی دکھاتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: محزاب عربی جڑ 'حَزَبَ' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے اکٹھا ہونا یا متحد ہونا۔ اردو میں، محزاب کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو فیصلے کرنے میں مضبوطی اور پختگی دکھاتا ہے، اور وہ شخص جو حق اور عدل کے ساتھ وفادار رہتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے ثقافت میں، محزاب کو ایک ایسے شخص کے طور پر سمجھا جاتا ہے جو اپنے اصولوں پر قائم رہتا ہے اور اپنے مقاصد کو حاصل کرنے کے لئے مستحکم رہتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुहज़्ज़ब
in_hindi.meaning: मुहज़्ज़ब वह व्यक्ति है जो निर्णय लेने में दृढ़ता और परिपक्वता दिखाता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुहज़्ज़ब अरबी मूल 'حَزَبَ' से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ है इकट्ठा होना या एकजुट होना। हिंदी में, मुहज़्ज़ब का अर्थ है वह व्यक्ति जो निर्णय लेने में दृढ़ता और परिपक्वता दिखाता है, और वह व्यक्ति जो सच्चाई और न्याय के साथ खड़ा रहता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, मुहज़्ज़ब को एक ऐसे व्यक्ति के रूप में देखा जाता है जो अपने सिद्धांतों पर अडिग रहता है और अपने लक्ष्यों को प्राप्त करने के लिए स्थिर रहता है।

in_english.name: Muhazzab
in_english.meaning: Muhazzab means one who is strong and resolute in decision-making
in_english.long_meaning: The name Muhazzab originates from the Arabic root 'حَزَبَ' (ḥazaba), which means to gather or collect. In the context of Islamic tradition, Muhazzab refers to someone who is strong and resolute in their decision-making, often standing firm for what is right and just. While the term is not directly mentioned in the Quran, the root 'ḥazaba' appears in several verses, emphasizing the importance of unity and collective action. Throughout Islamic history, the name Muhazzab has been associated with individuals known for their courage, determination, and commitment to justice. In contemporary Muslim cultures, the name continues to symbolize strength of character and moral integrity.

historical_references.reference: The Battle of Mu'tah (629 AD) was a major military engagement fought between the Muslim army under the command of Muhammad ibn Muslimah and the Byzantine and Ghassanid forces led by the Roman general, Al-Harith ibn Abi Shammas. The battle took place in the region of Mu'tah, in modern-day Jordan, and resulted in a decisive defeat for the Byzantines and Ghassanids. The name 'Muhazzab' is mentioned in Islamic tradition as the title given to Muhammad ibn Muslamah after this battle due to his bravery and determination in leading the Muslim troops to victory.
historical_references.context: Military engagement between Muslim and Byzantine/Ghassanid forces in Jordan

historical_references.reference: The Caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 AD) saw the expansion of the Islamic empire from the Arabian Peninsula to North Africa, the Levant, and Persia. One of the significant military campaigns during Umar's reign was the conquest of Egypt in 639 AD. The Islamic army was led by Amr ibn Al-As, who was given the title 'Al-Muhazzab' due to his military prowess and bravery during the campaign. The name 'Muhazzab' became a symbol of Islamic military strength and victory during this period.
historical_references.context: Military campaign to conquer Egypt and the use of 'Muhazzab' as a title for military commanders
